'''Gian-Luca Oppo''' (born 5 December 1958) is an Italian physicist, known for his work in laser physics and nonlinear and quantum optics. Currently based in [[Glasgow]], he holds the Chair of Natural Philosophy at the [[University of Strathclyde]].<ref name=":0">{{cite web |title=1796 Freeland Chair of Natural Philosophy |url=https://pureportal.strath.ac.uk/en/prizes/1796-freeland-chair-of-natural-philosophy/ |website=University of Strathclyde |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref>

== Education and career ==
Oppo was born in [[Modena]] in 1958, and grew up in [[Lodi, Lombardy|Lodi]] and [[Arezzo]]. He studied at the [[University of Florence]] and the National Institute of Optics, receiving his doctorate in physics in 1983<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://cnqo.phys.strath.ac.uk/people/academic-staff/gian-luca-oppo/|title=Gian-Luca Oppo – CNQO |website=University of Strathclyde |access-date= 18 September 2026}}</ref> under the supervision of [[Tito Arecchi]] and Antonio Politi.<ref>Oppo, G.-L., Politi, A., Lippi, G. L., & Arecchi, F. T. Frequency pushing in lasers with injected signal. Physical Review A, 34(5), 4000-4007 (1986). https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.34.4000</ref> He joined the [[University of Toronto]] in Canada in 1985 to work with Ray Kapral,<ref>Oppo, G.-L., & Kapral, R. Domain growth and nucleation in a discrete bistable system. Physical Review A, 36(12), 5820-5831 (1987).
https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.36.5820</ref> then [[Drexel University]] in Philadelphia in 1987, where he worked alongside [[L. M. Narducci|Lorenzo Narducci]] and Jorge Tredicce.<ref>Oppo, G.-L., Tredicce, J. R., & Narducci, L. M, Dynamics of vibro-rotational CO2 laser transitions in a two-dimensional phase space, Optics Communications, 69(5-6), 393-397 (1989). https://doi.org/10.1016/0030-4018(89)90026-6</ref> After a short period at the University of Nice (now [[Côte d%27Azur University]]) in 1989,<ref>Gil, L., Emilsson, K., & Oppo, G.-L. Dynamics of spiral waves in a spatially inhomogeneous Hopf bifurcation. Physical Review A, 45(2), R567-R470 (1992).
https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.45.R567</ref> he joined the Physics Department at the [[University of Strathclyde]] in Glasgow, Scotland, where he became Professor of Computational and Nonlinear Physics in 1998.<ref name=":1" /> Alongside Stephen Barnett and William Firth, he founded the Computational Nonlinear and Quantum Optics group, which was flagged 5* in the Research Assessment Exercise of 2001.<ref>{{cite web |title=RAE 2001 |url=http://www.rae.ac.uk/2001/ |website=Research Assessment Exercise |access-date=27 July 2026 |archive-url=https://webarchive.nationalarchives.gov.uk/ukgwa/20091118100740/http://www.rae.ac.uk/2001/ |archive-date=18 November 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> His chair was supported by [[Silicon Graphics|Silicon Graphics, Inc.]] from 2000 to 2005.<ref>Gomila, D., Zambrini, R., & Oppo, G.-L. Photonic Band-Gap Inhibition of Modulational Instabilities. Physical Review Letters, 92(25), 253904-1-4 (2004). https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevLett.92.253904</ref> Since 2015, Oppo has been the 1796 Freeland Chair in Natural Philosophy at Strathclyde.<ref name=":0" />

== Honours and recognitions ==
In 2011, Oppo was awarded the [[Institute of Physics Awards#Bilateral awards|Occhialini Medal and Prize]] from the [[Institute of Physics]] and the [[Italian Physical Society]], for "novel insights into nonlinear and quantum optical phenomena, especially spatio-temporal phenomena, achieved through the development and application of powerful techniques for small-scale computing".<ref>{{cite web |title="Giuseppe Occhialini" Prize |url=https://en.sif.it/prizes/occhialini_award |website=Società Italiana di Fisica |access-date=27 July 2026}}</ref> He is a fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://rse.org.uk/fellowship/fellow/professor-gian-luca-oppo-26595/|title=Professor Gian-Luca Oppo |website=Royal Society of Edinburgh |access-date= 18 September 2026}}</ref> the Optical Society of America (now [[Optica (society)| Optica]]),<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.optica.org/get_involved/awards_and_honors/fellow_members/fellows_search/|title=Fellows Search &#124; Optica|website=www.optica.org |access-date=18 September 2026}}</ref> and the Institute of Physics.<ref name=":1" />

* Politi, A., Oppo, G.-L., & Badii, R. Coexistence of conservative and dissipative behavior in reversible dynamical systems. Physical Review A, 33(6), 4055-4060 (1986). [https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevA.33.4055 Coexistence of conservative and dissipative behavior in reversible dynamical systems]
* Narducci, L. M., Scully, M. O., Oppo, G.-L., Ru, P., & Tredicce, J. R. Spontaneous emission and absorption properties of a driven three-level system. Physical Review A, 42(3), 1630-1649 (1990). * Livi, R., Franzosi, R., & Oppo, G.-L. Self-Localization of Bose-Einstein condensates in optical lattices via boundary dissipation. Physical Review Letters, 97, 060401 (2006). * Bao, H., Cooper, A., Rowley, M., Di Lauro, L., Totero Gongora, J. S., Chu, S. T., Little, B. E., Oppo, G.-L., Morandotti, R., Moss, D. J., Wetzel, B., Peccianti, M., & Pasquazi, A. Laser cavity-soliton microcombs. Nature Photonics 13, 384-389 (2019). [https://doi.org/10.1038/s41566-019-0379-5 Laser cavity-soliton microcombs]
* Oppo, G.-L. Computational physics applied to photonic devices. La Rivista del Nuovo Cimento 49, 1-74 (2026). [https://doi.org/10.1007/s40766-025-00077-0 Computational physics applied to photonic devices]
